item.title: Prayer of Saint James the Apostle to the Blessed Virgin of the Pillar
item.dc:creator: INFOVATICANA
item.description:
Prayer of Saint James the Apostle to the Blessed Virgin of the Pillar

Msgr. Alberto José González Chaves prays to the Blessed Virgin Mary, recalling his apostolic work in Spain and seeking her intercession. He reflects on his fiery nature as a son of thunder and expresses concern over the lack of progress in evangelizing the land. During his prayer, he hears the Angelic Salutation and sees the Virgin Mary, who encourages him to persevere and build a church dedicated to her. She promises that mercy will be shown through this church. More: InfoVaticana

item.title: At Least 139 Migrants Die in Boat Tragedy off Horn of Africa
item.dc:creator: Unknown
item.description:
At Least 139 Migrants Die in Boat Tragedy off Horn of Africa

A boat carrying over 300 migrants capsized off Djibouti, resulting in at least 139 deaths. The International Organisation for Migration reported that the shipwreck was one of the deadliest on the Eastern Route from the Horn of Africa to Yemen. Survivors described the vessel as overcrowded and sinking soon after departure. With 84 people still missing, the death toll is expected to rise. IOM Director-General Amy Pope called for action to prevent further tragedies. More: Vatican News

item.title: Rosario de Cristal to Return to Zaragoza Streets
item.dc:creator: INFOVATICANA
item.description:
Rosario de Cristal to Return to Zaragoza Streets

The Rosario de Cristal procession will take place in Zaragoza on Tuesday, October 13. Departing from the Church of the Sacred Heart of Jesus, it will feature monumental lanterns representing the mysteries of the Holy Rosary and pass through the historic center before returning to its starting point. This tradition, which dates back to the 19th century, combines Marian prayer with artistic heritage and extends devotions dedicated to Our Lady of the Pillar. The procession coincides with the month traditionally devoted to the Holy Rosary in the Catholic Church. More: InfoVaticana

item.title: Canada Halts Expansion of Assisted Suicide to People With Mental Illness
item.dc:creator: ZENIT Staff
item.description:
Canada Halts Expansion of Assisted Suicide to People With Mental Illness

Justice Minister Sean Fraser announced that Canada will not extend its assisted-dying program to people with mental illness. The decision, made in October 2026, maintains the current restriction on eligibility for medically assisted death. This move follows years of uncertainty and addresses concerns about assessing psychological suffering and safeguarding vulnerable groups. Critics argue that it recognizes the need for sustained treatment over immediate medical assistance. More: Zenit

item.title: Catholic Australians Remain Faithful Despite Irregular Attendance: Study Finds
item.dc:creator: Jorge Enrique Mújica
item.description:
Catholic Australians Remain Faithful Despite Irregular Attendance: Study Finds

A recent study commissioned by Australia’s Catholic bishops reveals that many Catholics who rarely attend Sunday Mass still hold strong beliefs and practices. The report, ‘Absent from the Table,’ surveyed 1,963 adult Catholics across seven states and found that 65% consider faith very important in their lives, with 44% sending children to Catholic schools. However, irregular attendance has declined significantly, with only 8.2% attending Mass weekly by 2021. The study identifies 14 reasons for this trend, including personal circumstances and dissatisfaction with Church life, suggesting the need for more community engagement and meaningful liturgy. More: Zenit

item.title: Celebrations for Saint Carlo Acutis Conclude in Assisi
item.dc:creator: info@domradio.de (DOMRADIO.DE)
item.description:
Celebrations for Saint Carlo Acutis Conclude in Assisi

On the anniversary of his death, Cardinal Luis Tagle concluded four days of festivities in Assisi dedicated to Saint Carlo Acutis by inviting young pilgrims to listen to Jesus’ call. The cardinal highlighted Acutis’s early recognition of the Eucharist as a path to heaven and warned against participating in worldly feasts that could lead to eternal damnation. The celebrations, which included special masses, musical performances, and eucharistic adoration, will end with an official closing mass on Monday, marking 20 years since Acutis’s death at age 15. More: Domradio

item.title: Synodal Process Emphasizes Relationship Building in European Churches
item.dc:creator: info@domradio.de (DOMRADIO.DE)
item.description:
Synodal Process Emphasizes Relationship Building in European Churches

Prof. Dr. Klara-Antonia Csiszar, organizer of the ‘Shaping Synodality in Europe’ conference, highlighted that synodal processes are about relationship-building at all levels of church governance. The conference, attended by 187 participants from 31 countries, focused on concrete steps for implementing synodality, including evaluating discussions and a questionnaire to identify themes and obstacles. Csiszar emphasized the importance of understanding diverse European experiences and suggested establishing an international forum to address current societal challenges. She warned against spiritualizing reform efforts without concrete actions. More: Domradio

item.title: Caritas Criticizes Personal Attacks Against German Labor Minister Bärbel Bas
item.dc:creator: info@domradio.de (DOMRADIO.DE)
item.description:
Caritas Criticizes Personal Attacks Against German Labor Minister Bärbel Bas

Caritas has condemned ‘inacceptable personal attacks’ against German Labor Minister Bärbel Bas (SPD), citing them as a reason for her resignation. Eva Welskop-Deffaa, Caritas president, stated that constant questioning of Bas’s efforts by the coalition partner hindered successful government policy-making. New SPD minister Alexander Schweitzer hopes his appointment will mark an era of compromise and mutual trust to ensure future social policies succeed. Bas cited the death of her stepdaughter and public attacks as reasons for stepping down from both party and cabinet positions, while retaining her parliamentary seat. More: Domradio

item.title: Doctors Recall Carlo Acutis’ Serene Final Days in Hospital
item.dc:creator: Courtney Mares
item.description:
Doctors Recall Carlo Acutis’ Serene Final Days in Hospital

Carlo Acutis, a 15-year-old who died from leukemia, was remembered by his doctors and hospital chaplain for his composure during his final days. Father Sandro Villa anointed him with the sick and gave him Communion before he fell into a coma. Carlo’s devotion to the Eucharist was evident throughout his life, as he built websites about miracles and went to daily Mass frequently. He is now a saint, canonized by Pope Leo XIV in 2025. More: EWTN News

item.title: 500th Anniversary of the Sacking of Rome: Commemorative Year for the Swiss Guard
item.dc:creator: Luigi Casalini
item.description:
500th Anniversary of the Sacking of Rome: Commemorative Year for the Swiss Guard

The Swiss Guard is commemorating the 500th anniversary of the Sacking of Rome in 2027. In 1527, 189 Swiss Guards died protecting Pope Clement VII while 42 survived to escort him to Castel Sant’Angelo. The commemorative year will run from January 23, 2027, with a historical conference, and culminate in May 2027 with Vespers, a Mass at St. Peter’s Basilica, and other events in Vatican City. Colonel Christoph Graf emphasizes the enduring values of loyalty, reliability, professionalism, and cohesion that these events symbolize for today’s Swiss Guard. More: Messainlatino
